classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the floor plan to identify the shelf's right angle, derive its equal base angles, and transfer the sloping-wall angle between parallel room boundaries before finding the table's supplementary vertex angle and equal base angles.

content.prompt: The diagram below is a plan of the first floor of Tony’s house.

spec.description: Unshaded floor plan with all room labels, one straight sloping outer wall, horizontal room partitions, the kitchen boundary, five right-angle marks, red dashed shelf and TV-table boundaries, and a curved leader identifying the TV table. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black; meaningful dashed boundaries retain house red.
spec.mathematics: The shelf is an isosceles right triangle. Its sloping side lies on the same straight outer wall as a side of the TV-table triangle. Horizontal boundaries are parallel through their perpendicular relationship to the left wall; the TV-table corner is supplementary to 45 degrees. No numerical angles, dimensions or equal-side ticks are supplied in the question figure.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels, boundaries and right-angle marks are permanent givens; numerical answers are absent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Tony would like to build some wooden shelves at the end of the recreation room. Each shelf would be an isosceles triangle. Find the internal angles of these shelves.

answer.worked:
The marked corner of each shelf is a right angle. The other two angles are equal because the shelf is an isosceles triangle.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Each remaining angle}&=(180^\circ-90^\circ)\div2\\\text{Each remaining angle}&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
The internal angles are $90^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $45^\circ$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Tony would also like to construct a TV table in the shape of an isosceles triangle in the living room. Evaluate the internal angles of the TV table.

answer.short:
$135^\circ$, $22.5^\circ$ and $22.5^\circ$.

Use the shelf’s $45^\circ$ angle and the straight outer wall, then use equal base angles.
answer.worked:
The recreation-room lower boundary and the living-room bottom boundary are parallel because both are perpendicular to the left wall. The straight sloping outer wall therefore makes the same acute angle, $45^\circ$, with each horizontal boundary. The table’s angle at the bottom-right corner is supplementary to this angle.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Table corner angle}&=180^\circ-45^\circ\\\text{Table corner angle}&=135^\circ\\\text{Each remaining angle}&=(180^\circ-135^\circ)\div2\\\text{Each remaining angle}&=22.5^\circ\end{align*}$$
The remaining angles are equal because the table is an isosceles triangle. Its internal angles are $135^\circ$, $22.5^\circ$ and $22.5^\circ$.
